_comment: On-device regression cases for the Dispatcharr TV player, driven headless through dispatcharrtv-* triggers in that install's runtime root (make -s print-rundir FLAVOR=<f>) and graded on dispatcharrtv-events.log there. Each case names a GENERATED clip (`make fixtures-pipeline`) served off the dev machine by tests/serve_fixtures.py, and the Load payload DECLARATION to play it with. `./tests/run.py` runs them. Nothing here is installation-dependent: no account, no server, no manifest.local.json -- only a TV address. The harness moves the set's Dispatcharr account aside for the run (and restores it), because a set with an account resumes its last channel on launch, and a tuned channel outranks the clip trigger.
_pipeline_declare_comment: `declare` is written verbatim into /tmp/dispatcharrtv-playurl (the harness injects `url`) and lands in route::set_stream_declaration, i.e. it IS the Load payload: `vcodec` picks the H265 vs H264 payload, `acodec` is renamed LG-side (eac3 -> "AC3 PLUS", aac -> "AAC", everything else -> "AC3"), `dovi` becomes the contents.DolbyHdrInfo node and `atmos` the contents.immersive one. `expect.load_*` grades what the app SAYS; `expect.codec` / `audio_stream_index` grade what the demuxer FOUND. The two are independent here, which is the whole point -- on the integration tier they both come from the same PMS metadata and can only ever agree.
_pipeline_skip_comment: A fixture the pack does not hold SKIPS its cases with the reason printed. So does a fixture generated SHORTER than the case seeks into it (checked with ffprobe), which would otherwise fail as though the player had regressed.
_resolution_matrix_comment:
LG App Self Checklist #50 / #51 is graded as a MATRIX of resolution x codec, and until 2026-08-23 this repo could only answer it as "pieces are covered": every fixture was 1080p except one 4K HEVC, so SD and HD had never been played at all and 4K H.264 existed in neither pack. The eight cells, all direct-play, all 24p, one audio codec per column so a row-to-row difference is the RESOLUTION and nothing else:

                    h264 / AC-3 5.1 mkv     hevc / E-AC-3 5.1 mkv
  SD    720x480     pipe_res_h264_sd        pipe_res_hevc_sd
  HD   1280x720     pipe_res_h264_hd        pipe_res_hevc_hd
  FHD  1920x1080    pipe_h264_ac3_1080p     pipe_res_hevc_fhd
  UHD  3840x2160    pipe_res_h264_uhd       pipe_hevc_eac3_4k_hdr10

Two cells predate the matrix and keep their names (`covers` carries `resolution-matrix` on them, so grepping that tag finds all eight). Every cell grades `expect.video_size` — an EXACT WxH out of the `ff:` line's AVCodecParameters, not a `min_video_width`, which cannot tell 720x480 from 720x576 and is how a matrix gets answered with "at least 1900 wide". The UHD/HEVC cell is HDR10 Main10 where every other cell is SDR 8-bit: HDR is a third axis, that cell is the one already device-verified (2026-08-22), and an SDR twin would differ from it only in `trc=`/`pri=`, which nothing here grades. Uncovered on purpose: the 4096-wide edge the device table claims and any refusal above it, and every non-24p rung (the frame-rate axis is pipe_h264_1080p5994 and pipe_hevc_4k_60fps, both at 1080p/4K only).

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_late_audio_eac3
pipeline_cases.title: E-AC-3 that starts 11 s after the video — the clock must still start and climb
pipeline_cases._note: The fixture carries NO audio packet for its first 11.008 s and ~16 MB of 12 Mbit/s video ahead of the first one (make_fixtures.py reads both back out of the finished file), which is more than the 10 MiB video lane. Two stalls stood behind each other: the demuxer parked on the full video lane before reaching the first audio packet, and then `feed_audio_lane` dropped the late audio as stale / the feed-ahead throttle held it, so no `feed a#` ever reached Starfish and the clock sat at 0. `min_pos_climb_s` is the whole-path symptom (a stalled clock climbs 0 s); `require_audio_feed_ready` (a `feed a#… reply=O` line) is the second stall on its own, so a fix for only the first cannot pass. `no_reload` keeps the stuck-clock watchdog's recovery reload from masking a stall as a late success. The 45 s cap leaves ~34 s of play after the audio exists and cannot reach this 60 s clip's EOS. Run on a television (webOS 4.10.2 family, debug flavour): it FAILED on the broken builds (main plus these tests: audio_feed, video_bound, pos_climb and presented_rate; the contributor's #603 as merged: audio_feed passed, the rest failed because the headroom was withdrawn too early) and PASSED on the build with the headroom held until the audio lead-in is pushed (all 11 assertions, 24.1 fps, 0 dropped).

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_res_h264_sd
pipeline_cases.title: SD 720x480 h264 + AC-3 — the smallest raster in the matrix
pipeline_cases._note: Square pixels, so the picture is 3:2 rather than the 4:3 a DVD displays. An anamorphic fixture would be grading PAR handling, which nothing in this repo asserts anywhere; see the matrix comment in make_fixtures.py.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_res_h264_uhd
pipeline_cases.title: UHD 3840x2160 h264 + AC-3 — the cell NEITHER pack could reach
pipeline_cases._note: 4K H.264 exists in no real library the maintainer has (every 4K item there is HEVC or AV1 — `library_gaps.video` lists it), so before this fixture the combination had never been played at all. The device's own capability table claims H.264 to 4096x2304@60, so this is inside the envelope, not at its edge.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_finish_eos
pipeline_cases.title: a 20 s clip played to its END — the completion half of LG #46
pipeline_cases._eof_note: One of the TWO cases in either tier that are supposed to run out — the other is `pipe_replay_after_eos` — and between them the only two allowed to name `pipe_h264_ac3_short.mkv`. Every other clip in both packs is sized so it CANNOT hit EOF inside a case's window (make_fixtures.py trap 9's second half), because a finish tears the session down under assertions that were only ever about playing; the rule is not "one case" but "a case graded through a teardown has to have declared `reaches_eos`", which tests/test_harness.py pins. run_secs is 60 against a 20 s clip: _resolve_fixtures SKIPS a `reaches_eos` case when the fixture is longer than 0.6 * run_secs PER VIEWING, so a pack regenerated with --secs/--quick skips it instead of failing it as a player regression.
pipeline_cases._replay_note: #46's REPLAY half is `pipe_replay_after_eos` below, which plays this same clip, lets it end, and starts it again. This case stays separate and grades the FINISH alone: the two failures are different — a stream that never ends, and a stream that ends and cannot be restarted — and collapsing them into one case would report either as the other.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_replay_after_eos
pipeline_cases.title: the same 20 s clip played to its end and then STARTED AGAIN — LG #46
pipeline_cases._replay_note: LG App Self Checklist #46, both halves, and the ONE case in either tier that plays the same media twice in one boot. `expect.replays` is the whole mechanism: the harness writes it into `/tmp/dispatcharrtv-replay`, and `app.rs` re-arms its one-shot `auto_tried` latch that many times when a `dispatcharrtv-playurl` playback reaches EOS — so the number the app is told and the number `a_replayed` grades cannot drift apart. A COUNTER rather than a lifted latch, because `auto_tried` also guards the autoplay+playidx arm, which fetches a catalog item; an unconditionally re-armable latch would loop a real playback forever.
pipeline_cases._wire_note: `server_opens_min: 2` is not decoration and is the assertion no log line can give. The second playback must fetch the clip AGAIN — `teardown` closed the socket and cleared the URL — so a 'replay' that somehow reused the first session's bytes would still satisfy the two `load:` lines and the position drop, and would be caught here, on the fixture server's own counter. It is a floor, not an equality: a `Range` reopen inside either viewing is permitted.
pipeline_cases._climb_note: `a_replayed` wants the position to FALL and then climb, which is the only signal that separates a restart from a session that carried on. A `min_pos_climb_s` of 8 alone cannot see it: one 20 s viewing satisfies that on its own, which is why the drop is asserted separately rather than by raising the climb floor to 30.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_h264_aac_resolution_spike
pipeline_cases.title: one Starfish Load: 720p -> 1080p -> 720p H.264/AAC
pipeline_cases._note: The file changes SPS/PPS/IDR in-band at media 8 s and 16 s while the case requires exactly one `load:` and forbids both app reload paths. Starfish type-4 source-info callbacks prove the coded-size sequence; GST is armed only for lxvideosink's per-picture cadence because the 5 Hz `vtick` heartbeat cannot measure frame-boundary stalls. `feed a#… reply=O` proves at least one AAC AU reached and was accepted by Starfish — readiness, not an assertion that a loudspeaker was audible. The 35 s cap observes both transitions plus 19 s of post-roll but cannot reach this 60 s clip's EOS. Exact server counters reject an invisible demux reopen just as exact Load count rejects an invisible Starfish replacement.
